statement: If I and I′ are finite posets, every u:I′→I is admissible; likewise under the stated noetherian sober hypothesis on I′^op.
repair: The comma shapes are lower subsets of I′, corresponding to closed subspaces of I′^op.
notes: The proposed more general poset case is finite for the reason just recorded.

statement: For admissible u, the functor induced by u_* on localizations of fibrant diagrams is right adjoint to u_W*.
repair: The Hom comparison is completed explicitly in commentary; the source’s final left/right wording is corrected only in the audit.
notes: The theorem statement has the right orientation.

statement: If the comma shapes are admissible and their restriction functors preserve fibrant objects, (Ru_*X′)_s≅R(p_s)_*q_s*X′.
repair: Compute both sides on a common fibrant replacement. For a discrete-fibration projection, fiberwise coproduct left Kan extension proves fibrant restriction when these coproducts exist.
notes: Historical pointwise Der5.

statement: A functor is strictly admissible when its comma categories I′/s are admissible.
repair: In the intended setting include the restrictions needed to compute the pointwise formula.
notes: The source has already invoked its local-isomorphism result for those restrictions.

statement: On finite posets the prederivator satisfies Der1, Der2, existence of right images, and the pointwise right-image formula.
gap_or_error: The assertion includes Der2 from §5, where strong saturation was explicitly assumed.
repair: Carry that inherited hypothesis or the equivalent saturation result of the homotopy calculus; do not silently erase it.
notes: Source uses historical Der4 and Der5 for the final two properties.

statement: If I has a greatest element a, then lim_I X≅X_a, so I is admissible whenever the diagram theory is defined.
repair: Because diagrams are contravariant, an object terminal in I is initial in I^op.
notes: No fibrancy is needed for this particular ordinary-limit functor to preserve W.

statement: A finite poset without a greatest element is the union of two proper lower subsets obtained by partitioning its maximal elements into two nonempty parts.
repair: Every element lies below a maximal one; the resulting lower sets and their overlap have smaller cardinality.
notes: The empty and singleton cases are handled separately.

statement: The two-open cover determines u:I→Ψ=(1←0→2), whose comma categories over 0,1,2 are the overlap and the two lower subsets.
repair: Send overlap to0 and each exclusive part to its corresponding vertex; lower-set closure ensures monotonicity.
notes: Explicit construction and ordinary pullback formula in p61 commentary.

statement: Composites of admissible functors are admissible.
repair: Right Kan extension preserves fibrant objects and (vu)_*≅v_*u_*.
notes: No extra choice of replacement is needed at this stage.

statement: The shape Ψ=(1←0→2) is admissible.
repair: Fibrant Ψ-diagrams are spans of fibrant objects with fibrant legs, and their ordinary pullbacks are homotopy invariant under the source’s properness axioms.
notes: This is the induction’s essential finite gluing lemma.

statement: A Ψ-diagram X_1→X_0←X_2 is fibrant iff all three values are fibrant and both legs belong to F.
repair: Choose the lift at X_0, then solve each remaining square against the corresponding leg fibration.
notes: The source’s unclear drawing is resolved as three vertical component maps, not extra arrows.

statement: A Ψ-diagram is trivially fibrant iff its three values are trivially fibrant and its two legs belong to TF.
repair: Use the same three-step lifting proof against objectwise cofibrations.
notes: The assumption includes maps from each value to the terminal object in TF.

statement: A map between cartesian squares whose corresponding pullback legs are W-fibrations is in W at the fourth corner if it is in W at the other three; one suitable leg in each square suffices.
repair: This is homotopy invariance of homotopy pullbacks; source M″ supplies the necessary properness condition. A complete chain-complex calculation is given in commentary.
notes: The source cites ChapterXIIp253, not available in this package.

statement: Noetherian induction on lower subsets reduces admissibility to the case in which every proper lower subset is admissible.
repair: A counterexample would generate an infinite strictly decreasing chain of lower subsets.
notes: Dependent choice or the equivalent minimal-counterexample principle is used.

statement: If I^op is irreducible and sober, I has a greatest element and is admissible.
repair: A generic point is a least element of I^op.
notes: This is the base case in the source’s topological induction.

statement: If I^op is reducible, it decomposes into two proper closed subsets, and admissibility follows by the two-open pullback argument on I.
repair: The proper lower subsets and their overlap lie below I in the induction order.
notes: The source’s proof is valid despite the vacuity of the supposed infinite extension.

statement: For a map of posets u:I′→I, each I′/s is a lower subset of I′ and its opposite is a closed subspace of I′^op.
repair: Closed subspaces of a noetherian sober space retain both properties.
notes: Used in theorem-scholie1(c).

statement: For cofibrant F and fibrant G′, Hom_W(u*F,G′) and Hom_W(F,u_*G′) are quotients of their ordinary Hom sets, related by the strict adjunction.
repair: Cofibrancy/fibrancy and the preceding homotopy calculus are the hypotheses.
notes: The display omits W-localizations on its right side; editors correct this in brackets.

statement: Even without admissibility, restriction followed by the counit gives a surjection Hom_W(F,u_*G′)→Hom_W(u*F,G′), natural in F for fixed fibrant G′.
repair: Strict adjunction supplies representatives, while restriction preserves W everywhere.
notes: Functoriality in the localized G′ variable has not yet been shown.

statement: Can the representing object of the preceding pointwise quotient be chosen functorially in localized G′ without admissibility?
repair: The manuscript does not establish this with weaker hypotheses. Under its eventual closed exact uniform hypotheses admissibility follows from Brown.
notes: Do not infer a general representability theorem from surjectivity alone.

statement: One may choose i′:u*F→F′ in TC with F′ fibrant and still cofibrant, and take its strict adjoint i:F→u_*F′.
repair: Factor u*F→e; stability of C under composition preserves cofibrancy.
notes: Construction used to recover the inverse Hom comparison.

statement: Precomposition by i′ gives Hom_W(F′,G′)≅Hom_W(u*F,G′).
gap_or_error: The source target has u*F′, which is not well typed.
repair: Read u*F; i′ is a weak equivalence and is inverted in the homotopy category.
notes: Edition slip retained in text and recorded separately.

statement: Admissibility makes u_* compatible with homotopy classes between fibrant objects, so the strict adjunction respects both Hom equivalence relations.
repair: Use γ(g)=u_*^W(a)∘[i], where a[i′]=g; both inverse identities are proved in commentary.
notes: The source proof is substantively correct once the typographical target is repaired.

statement: Representability of F↦Hom(HO(I′))(u*F,G′) gives a left adjoint of u*.
gap_or_error: The represented variable is contravariant in F and the representing object is the value of a right adjoint.
repair: Replace left by right; the theorem statement and displayed Hom bijection already have the correct orientation.
notes: First occurrence of adjoint à gauche on p71.

statement: The left adjoint just obtained is computed by u_* on fibrant G′.
gap_or_error: The same left/right reversal occurs a second time.
repair: The right adjoint is computed by u_* on fibrant representatives.
notes: Second occurrence of adjoint à gauche on p71.

statement: The comma projection I′/s→I′ is a local isomorphism and its restriction preserves fibrant objects in the applicable uniform diagram theory.
gap_or_error: For arbitrary infinite fibers in a merely finite-(co)complete category, the left-Kan construction needs its own existence hypothesis.
repair: For the finite-poset case fibers have size≤1; in cocomplete models prove preservation using fiberwise coproduct q_!.
notes: This is a prerequisite for the pointwise computation, not supplied by Brown alone.

statement: Do all functors u admit homotopy right images under the earlier large-category hypotheses; can a counterexample be found?
repair: Under the stated uniform closed exact structure, admissibility is automatic for every existing ordinary u_*. Any remaining obstruction is to existence of limits or structures.
notes: The source expresses doubt; it does not exhibit a counterexample.

statement: Is a small product of W-maps between fibrant objects again a W-map?
repair: Yes whenever the product exists and the product model structure is used: the diagonal is left Quillen and Brown applies to product.
notes: No filtered-colimit or accessibility hypothesis is required for this implication.

statement: Fibrant diagrams on N are inverse towers of fibrant objects with fibrations as bonding maps.
repair: Solve lifting problems recursively; this is the inverse-Reedy matching-object description.
notes: The category N has arrows n→n+1 while the coefficient diagrams are contravariant.

statement: Does inverse limit preserve levelwise W-maps between such fibrant towers?
repair: Yes: the constant-tower functor is left Quillen and the Brown argument applies to its right adjoint.
notes: A full nonfibrant acyclic-tower counterexample explains why the fibrancy qualifier matters.

statement: An affirmative answer for inverse towers implies an affirmative answer for countable products of fibrant objects.
repair: Express the countable product as the inverse limit of finite partial products, whose projections are fibrations.
notes: Complete reduction in p72 commentary.

statement: Can the product assertion fail even for a closed model category with the additional accessibility and filtered-colimit exactness hypotheses listed?
repair: No, if the products exist: Brown’s lemma settles it without those extra hypotheses.
notes: Question is answered positively for invariance, not left open in the audit.

statement: Is the one-object category BG admissible for a group G?
repair: Yes under the uniform closed exact hypothesis whenever the right Kan extension exists; ordinary fixed points must be taken on fibrant G-diagrams.
notes: Worked example calculates all Ext and Tor groups for C_p in characteristic p.

statement: Is the full subcategory of Δ on [0] and [1] admissible?
repair: Yes by the same Brown argument, given the assumed uniform diagram structure; its ordinary limit exists by M0.
notes: This full subcategory has two objects and seven morphisms, including sections, a retraction and endomorphisms; it is not the walking arrow.

statement: For the dual construction assume a closed right-exact structure with TF=F∩C.
gap_or_error: The printed intersection uses C instead of W.
repair: The intended assumption is TF=F∩W, as in M′_0(d) and the glossary.
notes: Source slip retained and corrected in audit, not in authoritative text.

statement: Assume C and TC are lifting closures of small generating sets C0 and TC0.
repair: Modern terminology is cofibrant generation, together with the required domain smallness for the small object argument.
notes: Source calls these left-closed classes accessible; footnote corrects right to left.

statement: Define F(I),TF(I) objectwise and C(I)=LLP(TF(I)), TC(I)=LLP(F(I)).
repair: This is the projective orientation of diagram model structures.
notes: The intended base equality uses W, not C.

statement: These classes should define a uniform right quillenisability on all small categories.
repair: True for locally presentable cofibrantly generated model categories; free diagrams on the generating maps and the small object argument construct it.
notes: A complete transfer explanation is supplied, with smallness hypotheses explicit.

statement: The remaining issue is factorization f=pi with i∈TC(I),p∈F(I), and with i∈C(I),p∈TF(I).
gap_or_error: The printed membership assertions name f rather than p.
repair: Use p in both; under suitable generation and smallness the two small object arguments supply the factorizations.
notes: Do not confuse a generating-set equality with a factorization theorem without smallness.

statement: It suffices to identify the right lifting classes as the prescribed pointwise classes and show the left lifting classes are generated by small sets.
repair: Use evaluation adjoints L_iA with components coproduct_{I(j,i)}A. Presentability of domains supplies the needed smallness.
notes: This is the substantive transfer problem, rather than another invariance problem.

statement: If the projective construction succeeds, left homotopy Kan extensions exist for maps of finite posets and the indicated noetherian sober extensions.
repair: The dual Brown argument gives all existing left Kan extensions once the projective structures exist. The stated noetherian sober posets are finite.
notes: Source draws this conclusion conditionally.

statement: Closure of W under filtered colimits should make discrete and left-filtered categories such as N^op admissible for left images.
repair: In the constructed projective model theory, dual Brown gives the conclusion; filtered-colimit closure separately explains certain direct computations.
notes: Do not identify arbitrary coproduct closure with filtered-colimit closure without the finite coproduct step.

statement: A poset which is a filtered union of closed noetherian sober subposets should be right-admissible under the projected dual hypotheses.
repair: With projective diagram structures and ordinary colimits, it follows from the general derived-left-Kan argument.
notes: The source is still conditional on the construction; the finite subposet condition does not address non-posets.

statement: What happens to left admissibility for BG?
repair: For the projective diagram model, derived coinvariants exist and are computed on cofibrant G-diagrams. The cyclic-group example gives nonzero Tor in every nonnegative homological degree.
notes: Answered in the standard model setting; no new obstruction from automorphisms remains.

statement: For an infinite cardinal pi, a nonempty poset is 'grand devant pi' if every subset of cardinal at most pi has an upper bound; equivalently it is pi^+-directed in modern terminology.
notes: Convention recalled from SGA 4 I 9.1 and explicitly restated in the glossary; successor shift retained throughout this audit.

statement: A cardinal filtration of a U-category E is an increasing family of replete full subcategories Filt^pi(E), indexed by infinite cardinals pi>=pi_0, satisfying (a), (b), (c) below.
notes: Filtration stages are not assumed presentable-object subcategories by this definition.

statement: Filtration axiom (a): each Filt^pi(E) is equivalent to a category belonging to the fixed universe U.
Filtration axiom (b): E admits colimits indexed by small pi_0^+-directed posets; Filt^pi(E) is closed under these colimits when the indexing poset has cardinal at most pi.
Filtration axiom (c): every X in E is a pi^+-directed colimit of objects of Filt^pi(E); if X belongs to Filt^{pi'}(E), pi'>pi, such an index can be chosen of size at most (pi')^pi.
If pi'=2^{c'} with c'>=pi infinite, then (pi')^pi=pi', so the preceding index can be chosen of size at most pi'.
notes: Correct cardinal arithmetic; no continuum hypothesis.

statement: Under GCH, (pi')^pi=pi' for every pair of infinite cardinals pi'>pi.
gap_or_error: Fails at singular pi' when cf(pi')<=pi.
repair: Retain the exponent bound or impose pi<cf(pi') in addition to GCH. Independently of GCH, Konig gives mu^{cf(mu)}>mu for singular mu; pi=aleph_0 and pi'=aleph_omega is a counterexample.
notes: The attached PDF prints the assertion. Source error, not transcription. Complete diagonal proof and corrected GCH statement in the commentary.

statement: Axioms (b) and (c) imply E=union_{pi>=pi_0} Filt^pi(E).
repair: Choose a presentation at pi_0 and a cardinal rho bounding its indexing set; use (b) at rho.
notes: Footnote 39; proof supplied, no missing mathematical hypothesis.

statement: For a pi^+-directed presentation X=colim_I X_i with X_i in Filt^pi, define P to be the inclusion poset of subsets S of I of size<=pi which are pi_0^+-directed, and Z_S=colim_S X_i.
Each Z_S exists and lies in Filt^pi(E).
notes: Direct application of L_{pi_0} and filtration axiom (b).

statement: The partial colimits Z_S form a covariant diagram over P, and |P|<=(|I|)^pi.
repair: Colimit functoriality and the bound on subsets of size at most pi.

statement: If |I|<=(pi')^pi, then |P|<=((pi')^pi)^pi=(pi')^pi.
notes: Uses pi infinite, hence pi*pi=pi.

statement: The poset P is pi^+-directed.
repair: The union of at most pi members has size<=pi; choose one upper bound in I and adjoin it. The resulting subposet has a largest element.
notes: The editorial bracket gives this shorter proof; no exponent assumption is needed.

statement: Lemma 1: if pi>=pi_0, I is pi^+-directed and S is a subset of size<=pi, then S lies in a pi_0^+-directed subposet S' of size<=pi.
repair: Take S'=S union {s} for an upper bound s of S in I.
notes: Editorial proof is complete. Footnote 40's additional assumptions are unnecessary for this statement.

statement: Editorial Lemma 1': if I is only pi_0^+-directed, pi>pi_0 and pi^{pi_0}=pi, every subset S of I of size<=pi lies in a pi_0^+-directed subposet of size<=pi.
repair: The transfinite construction runs through pi_0^+ stages; regularity ensures any <=pi_0 selected elements lie in one earlier stage.
notes: The source construction proves this stronger ambient-poset version. Its cardinal assumptions are sufficient rather than necessary.

statement: In the closure recursion S_{alpha+1} is obtained by adjoining upper bounds for all <=pi_0-element subsets of S_alpha not yet bounded there, and S_delta is the union at a limit ordinal delta.
notes: Every required upper bound exists in the ambient pi_0^+-directed poset.

statement: At alpha_0=pi_0^+ the union S_{alpha_0} is pi_0^+-directed.
repair: For at most pi_0 elements their chosen stage indices have supremum below regular pi_0^+; the next stage bounds them.
notes: Routine omitted verification supplied in commentary.

statement: Under pi^{pi_0}=pi and pi>pi_0, every closure stage through alpha_0 has size<=pi.
notes: Successor bound pi^{pi_0}; limit bound |alpha|*pi; final stage requires pi_0^+<=pi.

statement: The partial-colimit presentation (Z_S) indexed by P has colimit X.
repair: Cocones on the partial diagrams and on the original diagram correspond; singletons recover each original term, two-element subsets with a largest element recover transition compatibility.

statement: Every subset A of P of size<=pi which is pi_0^+-directed has a supremum in P.
repair: The supremum is the union; proof is Lemma 2.

statement: Lemma 2: a pi_0^+-directed union of at most pi many pi_0^+-directed subposets of size<=pi is again pi_0^+-directed and of size<=pi, assuming pi>=pi_0.
repair: A <=pi_0-element subset of the union lies in one member by directedness of the family, and has an upper bound there.
notes: The editor correctly removes pi>pi_0 and pi^{pi_0}=pi; in fact the union assertion does not need the ambient poset itself to be pi^+-directed.

statement: Proposition 1: every X admits a pi^+-directed presentation by Filt^pi objects in which each pi_0^+-directed subset J of the index of size<=pi has a supremum i_J and X_{i_J}=colim_J X_i. If X is in Filt^{pi'}, an index of size<=(pi')^pi can be used.
repair: Use the poset of small pi_0^+-directed subposets and partial colimits; cocones on a directed union identify the required colimit.
notes: The editorial weakening to pi>=pi_0 is valid; no exponent assumption is needed because the initial presentation is pi^+-directed.

statement: A presentation satisfying Proposition 1(a),(b),(c) is called well adapted to the cardinal filtration at (pi_0,pi).

If E admits all small filtered colimits and Filt^pi is closed under filtered colimits indexed by posets of size<=pi, one may instead index partial colimits by ordinary directed subsets S of I of size<=pi.
notes: This uses the bounded strengthened closure later named strictness. The preliminary prose and Proposition 1 bis phrase closure more strongly; the bounded hypothesis suffices.

statement: The poset of directed subsets of I of size<=pi is pi^+-directed, even if I is only an ordinary directed poset.
repair: Close any <=pi-element subset of I under chosen upper bounds for finite subsets through countably many stages; the resulting directed subset has size<=pi.

statement: Every ordinary directed family of at most pi members of this partial-subset poset has supremum its union.
notes: The union is directed and has size<=pi.

statement: The printed formula asserts Z_sup A ≅ lim_A Z_T for the covariant partial-colimit diagram.
gap_or_error: The printed formula uses an inverse-limit symbol, although both construction and text concern inductive limits.
repair: Read colim rather than lim in the formula; this is an edition/source slip retained in the transcription. The colimit equality follows from the universal property of a union of subdiagrams.
notes: The intended assertion is true; the literal displayed inference/formula is false in general.

statement: Proposition 1 bis: under strict bounded filtered-colimit closure, every X has a perfectly adapted presentation at pi: pi^+-directed index, Filt^pi terms, and continuity at suprema of directed index subsets of size<=pi.
notes: Printed statement assumes closure 'under these filtered colimits' without repeating the size bound, a stronger sufficient assumption. The footnote-41 bound is sufficient for the proof.

statement: A system as in Proposition 1 bis is called perfectly adapted; its presentation of X is a perfectly adapted representation.
A strict cardinal filtration is a cardinal filtration on a category admitting small filtered colimits whose stage Filt^pi is stable under filtered colimits indexed by posets of cardinal at most pi.
notes: Footnote 41 is the operative definition. The glossary later omits the size bound; that omission is audited separately by the appendix audit.

statement: For a replete class M of E-objects, M is pi-accessible relative to the strict filtration if for every perfectly adapted presentation X=colim_I X_i at pi, X belongs to M exactly when I_M={i:X_i in M} is cofinal in I.
notes: Repleteness is implicit in treating objects up to isomorphism. This is the source's b_pi condition, stronger at fixed pi than ordinary accessible inclusion.

statement: A cofinal subset I_M of a pi^+-directed poset is itself pi^+-directed and computes the same colimit; its terms belong to M^pi=M intersect Filt^pi.
repair: Bound at most pi indices in I, then move above the bound into I_M; use the elementary cofinality theorem for directed colimits.

statement: For any diagram X:I->E, I_M denotes {i in I:X_i in M}, and M^pi denotes M intersect Filt^pi.
notes: The editorial brackets correctly replace 'diagram in M' by 'diagram in E'.

statement: Condition a_pi: M is exactly the class of all colimits of pi^+-directed diagrams with values in M^pi.
notes: Includes both presentation of every M-object and closure for all such small-term diagrams.

statement: Condition b_pi: every perfectly adapted Filt^pi presentation detects membership of its colimit by cofinality of the indices whose terms lie in M.
notes: The word perfectly adapted includes that I is grand devant pi, even where the explanatory parenthesis abbreviates that clause.

statement: Condition c_pi: M^pi is strictly generating in the full subcategory M; M is closed in E under pi^+-directed colimits; for every X in M the category M^pi/X is ordinary filtered.
notes: Ordinary filteredness is weaker than pi^+-filteredness; strict generation is not silently replaced by mere generation.

statement: The three conditions a_pi, b_pi, c_pi are equivalent.
gap_or_error: Both a_pi=>b_pi and c_pi=>a_pi fail even when all Filt^pi objects are pi^+-presentable.
repair: Counterexamples in P(omega_1), pi=aleph_0: successor initial segments plus omega_1 satisfy a and c but not b; finite subsets plus omega_1 satisfy c but not a. Full proofs in the commentary. Replace c's ordinary filtered canonical slices by pi^+-filtered canonical slices to recover generation, not b at the same rank.
notes: Source says 'Je presume'. The present verdict uses explicit counterexamples, not a failure to find a proof.

statement: Condition b_pi implies that every X in M is a pi^+-directed colimit of objects of M^pi.
notes: Choose a perfectly adapted presentation and restrict to its cofinal M-part.

statement: Lemma 1: a_pi or b_pi implies M is closed under pi^+-directed colimits.
gap_or_error: The unqualified assertion is not established here; the subsequent Lemma 2 explicitly assumes presentability of the small filtration stage.
repair: Under Filt^pi subset E_pi the canonical-slice/Ind argument proves it; b=>a itself does not need that assumption. No unconditional counterexample is asserted in this audit.
notes: Do not label the unqualified statement false merely because the manuscript's proof changes hypotheses.

statement: To deduce membership of an arbitrary pi^+-directed colimit of M^pi-objects, it is enough to apply b_pi directly because I_M=I.
gap_or_error: The given presentation need not be perfectly adapted.
repair: The author retracts this inference in footnote 42 and repairs it on pp.96–97 by partial-colimit reindexing and a cofinal family of subposets with a largest element.
notes: The conclusion b=>a is true; this specific inference is invalid.

statement: Lemma 2: if every object of Filt^pi is pi^+-presentable in E, then a_pi, and hence b_pi, implies closure of M under pi^+-directed colimits.
gap_or_error: The manuscript's small-subcategory route has an insufficient image-cardinality bound on p.93 and leaves the canonical-slice lemma unproved.
repair: Use the complete canonical-slice proof and flattening argument in the commentary; alternatively SGA 4 I 9.18(a) realizes M as a full Ind_{pi^+} subcategory.
notes: The conclusion is correct under the displayed hypothesis. Hypothesis is present in Lemma 2, not a newly imposed restriction.

statement: For a pi^+-directed diagram X:I->M, C has objects (Z,i,alpha:Z->X_i) with Z in M^pi; an arrow is (u:Z->Z',i<=i') making the displayed square commute.
notes: This is the Grothendieck construction of the covariant diagram i |-> M^pi/X_i.

statement: C is the pullback of the target projection M^pi/E->E along X:I->E, with source functor Z:C->M^pi.
repair: Immediate from the specified object and arrow data.
notes: The diagram's label X |-> X_i should use i as variable; recorded as edition slip.

statement: The fibre C_i of C->I is M^pi/X_i.
notes: The source first prints Filt^pi/X_i and supplies the editorial correction M^pi/X_i; use the corrected intended statement.

statement: The presentation half of a_pi makes M^pi a strict generating subcategory of M and gives X_i=colim_{M^pi/X_i} Z.
gap_or_error: Presentability is needed to compare an arbitrary map Z->X_i with the chosen presentation. The editors flag the unsupported general inference.
repair: Under the hypothesis of Lemma 2, every such map factors through a presentation term, and any <=pi relations become equal at a common later stage. This proves canonical density and even pi^+-filteredness of the slice.

statement: The target projection M^pi/E->E and its pullback C->I are opfibrations, and the colimit of Z over C is the iterated colimit over its fibres, hence colim_I X_i.
repair: A morphism in E transports (Z->X) by postcomposition. Cocones on C are compatible fibrewise cocones; their universal property proves the iterated-colimit identity.
notes: The source calls the opfibration proper in its ordinary-colimit vocabulary; no modern model-category properness assertion is intended.

statement: Assuming a_pi, the displayed fibrewise colimit description already proves colim_I X_i belongs to M.
gap_or_error: One still must show the total index C is pi^+-filtered (not only ordinary filtered) and replace it cofinally by a pi^+-directed poset.
repair: Under Lemma 2's compactness hypothesis, each fibre is pi^+-filtered; a <=pi diagram in C can be pushed to one fibre and given a cocone there. Cofinal poset replacement then applies a_pi.
notes: Footnote 43; correct conclusion with an omitted directedness argument.

statement: Define tilde C_i as the inclusion poset of filtered subcategories C_i' of C_i for which card Z(C_i')<=pi.
gap_or_error: A bound on the image category of the diagram does not bound the index or the size of its filtered colimit.
repair: For the construction to serve its stated purpose, require at most pi morphisms in the indexing subcategory itself, or use directed indexing posets of size<=pi.
notes: Exact image-cardinality notation is printed in PDF leaf 22; retained as a source issue.

statement: Lemma: under b_pi, or the presentation half of a_pi, and presentability of the Filt^pi objects, M^pi/X is filtered for every X in M.
repair: Proved in the commentary, with stronger conclusion pi^+-filtered. Factor maps through a chosen pi^+-directed presentation and equalize at most pi relations at a later stage.
notes: Source explicitly says 'J'admets'; footnote 44 identifies presentability. This is a genuine omitted proof, not an incorrect theorem.

statement: Every object and arrow of C_i is contained in a small filtered subcategory, so the union of the subcategories used in the corrected tilde C_i is C_i.
repair: Close a finite or <=pi collection of objects/arrows under identities, composition and cones for finite diagrams through countably many stages.
notes: Use the corrected bound on indexing morphisms; fullness is not required.

statement: The corrected small-filtered-subcategory poset tilde C_i is pi^+-directed and admits suprema of directed subfamilies of size<=pi, given by unions.
gap_or_error: The literal image-bound formulation does not supply the bounded-index argument.
repair: With |Mor C_i'|<=pi, close the union of <=pi subcategories under finite cocones. For a directed family, the union is already filtered and has the same size bound.

statement: The total poset tilde C consists of pairs (i,C_i'), ordered by i<=j and containment of the transported subcategory in C_j'. Its projection has target I.
gap_or_error: The printed displayed projection incorrectly has target C.
repair: Read p:tilde C->I, as required by the order relation and the stated fibres.
notes: Edition/source slip confirmed visually in leaf 22; not silently altered in source.

statement: The corrected total poset tilde C is pi^+-directed.
repair: Move <=pi pairs to a common index of I and enlarge the union of their transported small subcategories to a filtered subcategory with <=pi morphisms.

statement: For every C_i' admitted by the printed image-size definition, Z_{C_i'}=colim_{C_i'} Z belongs to Filt^pi(E).
gap_or_error: Image size does not control indexing size.
repair: In Set at pi=aleph_0, injections n->X from standard finite sets into an uncountable X form a filtered category whose source image is countable, while the colimit is X. Bound indexing morphisms by pi instead; bounded filtered-poset replacement then makes filtration closure applicable.
notes: Full counterexample and corrected construction in development commentary.

statement: With the printed tilde C_i, the diagram (Z_{C_i'}) is perfectly adapted at pi.
gap_or_error: Its values need not belong to Filt^pi, by the preceding counterexample.
repair: Use the corrected indexing-cardinality bound. Directed-union suprema then make the partial-colimit diagram continuous and its values lie in Filt^pi.

statement: The colimit of the corrected partial-colimit diagram over tilde C_i is X_i.
repair: Its small subcategories cover C_i and every finite compatibility datum occurs in one; identify cocones and use the canonical presentation X_i=colim_{C_i} Z.

statement: Applying b_pi to each corrected fibre shows that its subposet of partial colimits belonging to M^pi is cofinal.
gap_or_error: Literal use of b_pi before correcting the size condition is invalid, because the claimed presentation need not be perfectly adapted.
repair: After the indexing-size correction this is exactly b_pi, using X_i in M.
notes: The intended inference is sound and requires no extra hypothesis beyond the preceding repaired construction.

statement: The union over all fibres of the good partial-colimit indices is cofinal in the total poset tilde C.
repair: For a pair (i,D), choose a good larger subcategory in that same fibre.

statement: The corrected total partial-colimit diagram and its cofinal good subdiagram both have colimit X=colim_I X_i.
repair: Combine the fibrewise colimit identity, the Grothendieck-construction cocone calculation and cofinality.

statement: The resulting cofinal good diagram presents X as a pi^+-directed colimit of M^pi-objects, but is not known to be perfectly adapted.
notes: Cofinal restriction preserves pi^+-directedness but need not preserve small directed suprema or continuity there. The source correctly refuses to apply b_pi directly.

statement: If a_pi is assumed, this small-term presentation is enough to conclude X belongs to M.
notes: Footnote 45; use a_pi after correcting the preceding construction. This is the closure conclusion of Lemma 2.

statement: For X=colim_I X_i with I pi^+-directed and X_i in M^pi, reindex by P={nonempty directed subsets S of I of size<=pi}, with Z_S=colim_S X_i; this gives a perfectly adapted presentation at pi.
repair: Bounded strictness gives stage membership; unions give suprema and continuity; cocones show the same total colimit.

statement: The subposet P_0 of directed subsets having a largest element is cofinal in P, and Z_S is in M^pi for S in P_0.
repair: For S choose an upper bound s in I and use S union {s}; its colimit is X_s.

statement: By b_pi, the cofinality of P_M implies X belongs to M, completing b_pi=>a_pi.
notes: The source's own complete repair of the invalid p.90 inference.

statement: The implication b_pi=>a_pi does not use presentability of the Filt^pi objects; the presented proof of closure under arbitrary pi^+-directed diagrams in M does use it.
notes: Correct separation of hypotheses; preserve it when modernizing the argument.

statement: Condition a_pi implies the sufficiency half of b_pi: if I_M is cofinal in a perfectly adapted pi-presentation, then its colimit lies in M.
notes: The cofinal subset is pi^+-directed and its values lie in M^pi.

statement: For the proposed converse a_pi=>b_pi, assume Filt^pi(E) consists of pi^+-presentable objects of E.
notes: This is explicitly admitted in the source; it is insufficient for a_pi=>b_pi at the same rank, as the powerset example shows.

statement: If X has both a perfectly adapted Filt^pi presentation and a pi^+-directed presentation by M^pi-objects, can one show its adapted M-stages cofinal?
repair: Negative at the same rank: the successor/limit-ordinal counterexample in the commentary has precisely these properties.
notes: Open here in the source; not open after the explicit counterexample. The audit keeps the question's source status.

statement: After replacing pi by a larger cardinal pi' (suggested pi'=pi^+), a_pi should imply b_{pi'}.
gap_or_error: The printed target is b_pi again, inconsistent with the preceding enlargement; the intended larger-rank statement is not proved before the chapter ends.
repair: The commentary proves a_pi=>b_{pi^+} assuming Filt^pi objects pi^+-presentable and Filt^{pi^+} objects pi^{++}-presentable. This conditional completion uses no GCH and is separate from the source fragment.
notes: Do not assert that the filtration axioms alone supply either presentability assumption; do not silently amend the source display.

gap_or_error: The chapter ends after 'et des homomorphismes'; neither the full compatibility conditions nor the conclusion or proof survives here.

statement: M0: The category \mathcal M has all finite limits and finite colimits.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M1: C\perp TF and TC\perp F: every commutative square with left map in C and right map in TF, or left map in TC and right map in F, admits a diagonal filler.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M2: Every morphism f factors as p i with i\in C,p\in TF, and also as q j with j\in TC,q\in F; no functorial choice is asserted.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M3: F is closed under composition and pullback, C under composition and pushout, and both contain all isomorphisms.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M4: TF is closed under composition and pullback, TC under composition and pushout, and both contain all isomorphisms.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M5: W contains all isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three for composable arrows f,g and gf.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98. Retract closure is not stated in this axiom.

statement: M': TC\subset C\cap W and TF\subset F\cap W.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M'': C\subset\mathrm{Cof}_W and F\subset\mathrm{Fib}_W, with the intrinsic universal pushout/pullback conditions defined in the glossary.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98. This is the properness-type condition built into Grothendieck's weak structures; it is not an automatic axiom of an arbitrary modern model category.

statement: M'_0(g): TC=C\cap W (left exactness).
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M'_0(d): TF=F\cap W (right exactness).
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98.

statement: M2bis: W=TF\circ TC, meaning that f\in W exactly when f=p i for some i\in TC and p\in TF.
notes: Edition appendix, Liste des axiomes; attached PDF leaf 29, printed p.57. This is a restatement of the chapter's earlier axioms, not an additional theorem proved on manuscript pp.51–98. This is the exactness required by quillenisability; it is stronger than merely having TC,TF contained in W.

statement: A class \Phi of maps is closed on the left if \Phi={}^\perp\Psi for some class \Psi; that is, membership is characterized by the left lifting property against all maps of \Psi.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 1; attached PDF leaf 30, printed p.58. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A class \Psi of maps is closed on the right if \Psi=\Phi^\perp for some class \Phi; that is, membership is characterized by the right lifting property against all maps of \Phi.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 1; attached PDF leaf 30, printed p.58. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A pair (\Phi,\Psi) has the Quillen factorization property if \Phi\perp\Psi and every map f has a factorization f=p i with i\in\Phi and p\in\Psi.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 1; attached PDF leaf 30, printed p.58. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. No functorial factorization is required.

statement: A Quillen pair is a pair with the Quillen factorization property such that \Phi is closed on the left and \Psi is closed on the right; equivalently it is a weak factorization system.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 1; attached PDF leaf 30, printed p.58. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The equality with the mutual lifting classes follows from factorization and the retract argument.

statement: W is weakly saturated in this chapter if it contains all isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 30, printed p.58. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. This terminology must not be confused with modern weak saturation meaning closure under pushouts, transfinite composition and retracts.

statement: A map p:X\to Y belongs to \mathrm{Fib}_W if for every Y'\to Y and every w:Y''\to Y' in W, the induced map X\times_Y Y''\to X\times_Y Y' belongs to W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 30–31, printed p.58–59. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The two displayed squares are pullbacks. This is an intrinsic condition relative to W, not the chosen lifting class F.

statement: A map i:A\to B belongs to \mathrm{Cof}_W if for every A\to A' and every w:A'\to A'' in W, the induced map B\amalg_A A'\to B\amalg_A A'' belongs to W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 31, printed p.59. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The two displayed squares are pushouts. This is the dual intrinsic condition, not the chosen lifting class C.

statement: A map p:X\to Y is universally in W (p\in W_{\mathrm{univ}}) if every pullback of p belongs to W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 31, printed p.59. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A map i:A\to B is co-universally in W (i\in W^{\mathrm{univ}}) if every pushout of i belongs to W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 31, printed p.59. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. Superscript and subscript distinguish the dual notions; the superscript in the transcription agrees with the PDF.

statement: A left pre-Q model category, also called left pre-Quillen, is (\mathcal M,W,C,F,TC,TF) satisfying M0–M5, M', M'', and TC=C\cap W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A right pre-Q model category, also called right pre-Quillen, is (\mathcal M,W,C,F,TC,TF) satisfying M0–M5, M', M'', and TF=F\cap W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: The glossary uses Q-model category and Quillen triple for a model category in Quillen's original sense; this name is not the chapter's much weaker datum (\mathcal M,W).
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The source delegates to Quillen's definition. Historical 'closed' is recorded separately in the next row; neither small-limit completeness nor functorial factorization is silently added.

statement: Closed Q-model category, closed Quillen triple, closed Quillen category and closed Quillen system are synonyms for a closed model category in Quillen's original terminology, with the lifting classes determined by the corresponding lifting properties.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The source's distinct historical terms are retained; modern usage usually incorporates the closed/retract conditions into 'model category'.

statement: A closed pre-Quillen quintuple is (W,C,F,TC,TF) satisfying M0–M5, M', M'', with C and TC closed on the left and F and TF closed on the right.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A weak Quillen system is (W,C,F,TC,TF) satisfying M0–M5, M', M''.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A left exact weak Quillen system is a weak Quillen system satisfying TC=C\cap W; a right exact one satisfies TF=F\cap W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 2; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The glossary states the two dual definitions together.

statement: A category of models (\mathcal M,W) in this chapter means a category with finite limits and colimits and a class W containing isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. It has no specified cofibration or fibration class until a Quillen structure is supplied.

statement: A weak Quillen structure on (\mathcal M,W) is a quadruple (C,F,TC,TF) satisfying M1–M5, M', M''; M0 is already required of the underlying pair.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The glossary writes (C,F,TC,TF), while the main text often writes (C,TC,F,TF); the class names, not tuple positions, determine their roles.

statement: A weak Quillen structure is exact if it also satisfies W=TF\circ TC (M2bis).
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A weak Quillen structure is left exact if TC=C\cap W and right exact if TF=F\cap W.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 32, printed p.60. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A weak Quillen structure is closed on the left when C and TC are left lifting classes, and closed on the right when F and TF are right lifting classes.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 33, printed p.61. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A weak Quillen structure is closed when it is closed on both sides.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 33, printed p.61. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index.

statement: A Quillen structure is a biexact weak Quillen structure, meaning TC=C\cap W and TF=F\cap W; the glossary identifies this with a proper Quillen model structure.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 33, printed p.61. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. Properness comes from M''. The source uses Quillen's historical finite-(co)limit convention and keeps closedness as a separate condition.

statement: A perfect Quillen structure is a closed biexact weak Quillen structure; the glossary identifies this with a proper closed Quillen model structure.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 3; attached PDF leaf 33, printed p.61. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The finiteness convention of M0 is retained; no assertion that all small limits exist is added.

statement: The glossary states that a strict cardinal filtration has every stage \mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}(E) closed under all filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: It omits the cardinal bound from manuscript p.86, footnote41. Taken literally with the representation axiom, this forces \mathrm{Filt}^{\pi}(E)=E for every \pi and E essentially small.
repair: Read closure under filtered colimits indexed by categories of cardinality at most \pi, as the manuscript's explicit definition says; retain the printed glossary wording in the source.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 7; attached PDF leaf 35, printed p.63. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. The definition from ms.86 itself is audited in the main-text register. This row audits the inconsistent appendix reformulation.

statement: The final glossary paragraph calls a perfectly adapted representation the colimit of a 'well adapted' system.
gap_or_error: The adjective is inconsistent with the immediately preceding definition of perfectly adapted system and weakens the stated continuity condition.
repair: Replace 'well adapted' by 'perfectly adapted' when interpreting this definition; preserve the printed word in the source.
notes: Edition appendix Glossaire, Section 7; attached PDF leaf 35, printed p.63. Main chapter locations in this row follow the edition's notation/terminology index. This is an editorial cross-definition slip, not a new mathematical theorem.
